findings.body: The new `remindersToCancel` query selects `prisma.workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().add(1, "hour") } } })` without filtering on `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` or `scheduled: true`. For EMAIL reminders without a `referenceId` (unscheduled, `scheduled: false`), `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` deletes the row; for those with a `referenceId` it only sets `cancelled: true`. Because nothing is awaited, the mutation continues and eventually returns the updated workflow while these operations are still in flight; if the process crashes or the event loop is saturated, rows may be left in an inconsistent state (e.g. `cancelled` not yet persisted, or row deleted while SendGrid send still active for the SMS path). The same un-awaited `forEach` pattern appears at lines 212 (workflow delete), 519 (step delete), and 574 (step edit). All of these should collect promises and `await Promise.all(...)` before proceeding, and the workflow delete path should await cancellation before `ctx.prisma.workflow.deleteMany` removes the workflow (and cascades the reminder rows), otherwise the cascade can delete reminder rows before the SendGrid/Twilio cancellation has been recorded.

findings.title: deleteScheduledEmailReminder deletes the row when referenceId is null, but for a scheduled reminder whose referenceId was lost the SendGrid send is never cancelled
findings.body: When `referenceId` is null/empty, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` immediately deletes the `workflowReminder` row and returns. For a reminder that was actually scheduled in SendGrid (row has `scheduled: true`) but whose `referenceId` was never persisted or was lost, this deletes the only record of the scheduled send without calling SendGrid to cancel it, so the email will still be delivered. This is a defensive-coding gap: the function should distinguish 'never scheduled' (`scheduled === false`, safe to just delete) from 'scheduled but referenceId missing' (should attempt cancellation by other means or at least log loudly / not silently delete). As written, any data-integrity issue with `referenceId` silently converts into 'reminder email still sent', which is the exact failure mode this PR is fixing.

findings.title: CRON cleanup deletes past-due EMAIL reminders regardless of `scheduled` flag, racing with the scheduling loop
findings.body: The first statement of the handler, `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL, scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().toISOString() } } })`, deletes every EMAIL reminder whose scheduledDate has passed, including rows with `scheduled: true` whose SendGrid send may not have been delivered yet (SendGrid delivers at `sendAt`; clock skew or a slightly early CRON run can delete the row before SendGrid fires). It also deletes rows with `scheduled: false` that the same handler run is about to process further down (the `unscheduledReminders` query uses `scheduledDate <= now + 72h`, which includes past-due unscheduled rows). Deleting a `scheduled: true` row removes the record needed to cancel the send if the booking is cancelled in the window between the delete and the actual SendGrid delivery. The cleanup should be restricted to rows that are actually past and no longer actionable (e.g. `scheduled: true` and `scheduledDate` well in the past, or `cancelled: true`), and should not race with the scheduling query in the same run.
